FILE: CAL-A.txt
Title: Automatic quarantine for repeatedly flaky tests
We keep a rolling 14-day record for each test. If a test both passes and fails on
the same commit in at least 3 of the last 20 runs, we move it to a quarantine
suite that still runs nightly but does not block merges. A ticket is filed
automatically. The test leaves quarantine after 20 consecutive passes.
Test of the idea: turn it on for one repository for two weeks and count blocked
merges before and after. Cost: one nightly job.
FILE: CAL-B.txt
Title: Retry failed tests with growing delays
When a test fails, run it again up to three times, waiting 5, 15, then 45
seconds between attempts. If any retry passes, report the test as flaky-pass and
let the build continue. If all retries fail, fail the build.
Test of the idea: enable on one pipeline and compare red-build rate over two
weeks against the previous two weeks. Cost: up to 65 extra seconds per failure.
FILE: CAL-C.txt
Title: Flaky-test dashboard
Collect pass/fail history for every test into a web page. Show a table sorted
by flip rate (fraction of runs whose result differs from the previous run),
with red/yellow/green badges and a 30-day sparkline per test. Engineers open
the page during triage to see which tests flip most.
Test of the idea: give the page to one team for a month and ask whether triage
got faster. Cost: one small web service.
FILE: CAL-D.txt
Title: Pin the random seed per test file and record it
Each test file gets a fixed seed derived from its path, passed to the test
runner, and printed in the build log. When a test fails, anyone can rerun the
exact same random sequence locally with one flag using the printed seed.
Test of the idea: take 10 past flaky failures, rerun each with its recorded
seed, and count how many reproduce. If fewer than 5 reproduce, drop the idea.
Cost: a small runner patch.

item.text: The examples cover quarantine, retries, a dashboard, and seed control. I’ll score concrete usefulness separately from evidence of novelty, then combine the points. Novelty credit will require an explicit comparison and a specified mechanism, so graders won’t need to judge originality from memory.
